claims.claim: newMux only registers GET /{$}; there is no /healthz route today.

scenario.then: the response is 405, since only GET is registered for the route

overview.objective: Add a health check endpoint so a load balancer can tell when Zing is ready to take traffic.
overview.context: cmd/zing/main.go builds the HTTP server and its routes in newMux; this adds one more GET route beside the existing index handler.
overview.problem: Nothing today answers a liveness probe, so an operator has no cheap way to ask "is this process up."

goals.goal: GET /healthz returns 200 with a short body when the process is running

nongoals.nongoal: Checking downstream dependencies (database, disk) is out of scope; this is a process liveness check, not a readiness check

design.demo: Starting the server and curling /healthz prints "ok" with a 200 status, showing the route is live end to end.
design.shape: newMux gains one more route, `GET /healthz`, registered beside the existing `GET /{$}` route. Its handler writes a 200 status and a fixed "ok" body; it needs no dependencies, so it stays a package-level function like index.

files.file: register the /healthz route in newMux and add its handler
add TestHealthz covering GET and the POST 405 case

tests.test: GET /healthz returns 200 and body "ok"; POST /healthz returns 405

tasks.task: Add the /healthz handler and register it in newMux so the demo command above returns 200.

alternatives.alternative: Reuse the index handler for /healthz too: rejected, since a load balancer probe should not depend on the same path or body as the human-facing page.

risks.risk: A load balancer configured to expect a different status code or body would need reconfiguring; call this out in the PR description.
